inferred_rule: `NS1_T0`/`NS1_T6` = one patient, two draws; NS = non-survivor
authoritative_patient_key: sample-title prefix before the T0/T6 token (repository has no separate patient field)
draw_meaning: T0 = 0 h post sepsis diagnosis; T6 = 6 h post sepsis diagnosis (within-subject design)
outcome_availability: encoded in the sample label itself: S1-S3 survived and were discharged from ICU; NS ES and NS LS had fatal courses
corrections: titles are `NS ES_T0/T6`, `NS LS_T0/T6`, `S1 T0/T6`, `S2_T0/T6`, `S3_T0/T6`, `HC1`, `HC2` - there is no `NS1`/`NS2`; note the first two pairs use a space, the rest an underscore
residual_gaps: none for grouping; per-patient clinical detail beyond survivor/non-survivor not in the repository record

verdict: CONFIRMED for the bulk records; DOES NOT APPLY to the single-cell libraries
authoritative_patient_key: HGR subject id in the sample title (bulk RNA-seq records only)
draw_meaning: up to four draws per patient, T0 at or near hospital admission; draw times span a range of days post symptom onset rather than fixed intervals
anchor: hospital admission (T0), reported against days post symptom onset
outcome_availability: not in the GEO record (severity/outcome are in the paper's supplementary tables)
corrections: of 241 samples in the series, 71 are per-subject bulk RNA-seq (`Batch N bulk RNAseq HGR0000071`, timepoint Timepoint 0-3) and 170 are 10x lanes (`Batch N PBMC 10x Lane N ...`) whose `timepoint` value is literally `mixed` - the single-cell libraries are multi-subject pools and carry no HGR id, so no title-based patient assignment is possible for them
residual_gaps: donor identity for the 168 pooled single-cell lanes requires genotype/hashtag demultiplexing metadata not present in the GEO record

verdict: CONFIRMED for grouping; day anchor INFERRED (not stated in the deposit)
authoritative_patient_key: EGA `subject_id` (C19-CB-*, BN-*), retrieved from the EGA metadata API
authoritative_draw_key: subject_id + day suffix (suffix strings are not present in EGA - sample titles are null)
draw_meaning: repeat draws across the hospital course; cohort 1 sampled day 3-20 after symptom onset, cohort 2 day 2-25 after symptom onset
anchor: symptom onset (per the paper's own reporting for both cohorts)
outcome_availability: not in EGA metadata (phenotype field carries disease/severity only)
corrections: the C19-CB subject set contains exactly 27 samples across 18 subjects, matching the paper's cohort-1 statement of 27 samples from 18 patients - this is what confirms subject-level grouping; 16 further entries have subject_id `pooled_*` (e.g. pooled_200416) and are multiplexed libraries that cannot be attributed to one subject
residual_gaps: EGA sample titles are null, so the `_dN` strings themselves are unverifiable from the deposit; the day anchor is inferred from the paper's day-after-onset reporting, never stated as a naming convention

authoritative_patient_key: `patient_id` (CV0052, MH9179824, ...) = the SECOND token; the first token BGCVnn is the 10x sequencing pool
draw_meaning: Collection_Day D0 (Initial) vs D28 (Resample) for 12 patients; 1 healthy donor (CV0902) appears in two pools on the same day, i.e. a duplicate library rather than a second draw
anchor: D0 = first study draw; Days_from_onset is recorded once per patient at the initial draw and is NOT the time of the D28 draw
outcome_availability: `Outcome` in the processed object obs: Home / Death / unknown, and it is unique within every one of the 130 patients (8 patients have Outcome = Death)
corrections: 15 pools x exactly 4 donors each; 13 of the 15 pools contain more than one distinct Outcome. Grouping by the BGCVnn token therefore manufactures the mixed-outcome artefact: pool BGCV02 holds CV0052 (Death) plus CV0059, CV0068, CV0902 (all Home)
residual_gaps: none for the grouping question; the SDRF alone gives individual and sequence pool but no outcome - outcome required reading the published object's obs

verdict: CONFIRMED as visit codes, NOT replicates
authoritative_patient_key: `patient number` characteristic (001-014) in GEO; `PC_<n>` in the sample title
draw_meaning: visits after hospital admission: TA day 1, TA2 day 3, TB day 8, TB2 day 11, TC day 14, TE day 20 (figure legend). Codes `TD` (2 samples) and `rec` (2 patients, recovery/discharge) also occur in the deposit and are not defined in the paper
outcome_availability: `remission` characteristic per sample in GEO; the paper reports 3 ARDS patients of whom 2 had fatal courses
corrections: the two statements in the paper disagree by one day: the methods give the scheme as day 0 (admission), 2, 7, 10, 13 and/or discharge, while the figure legend maps the same visit codes to days 1, 3, 8, 11, 14, 20 - treat the day numbers as nominal visit days, not measured intervals
residual_gaps: GSE161777 is the whole-blood bulk RNA-seq/BCR deposit; the single-cell data are hosted on FastGenomics, which was not retrieved, so per-cell sample labels were not checked against these records

inferred_rule: each bare GSM accession = one patient
verdict: CORRECTED - 6 of 38 libraries are multi-patient pools
authoritative_patient_key: the patient/donor number named in the sample title (`10X GEX library for Patient 12`)
authoritative_draw_key: patient number (single draw per subject in this deposit)
draw_meaning: one library per subject except for 6 pooled libraries; no subject is sampled twice
anchor: not reported in the repository record
outcome_availability: `covid_status` (POSITIVE/NEGATIVE) and `phenotype` per sample; outcome as such not reported
corrections: pooled libraries carry 2-3 patients each (Patients 1+2+3; 5+6; 7+8+9; 10; 17+20+21; 50+51) with covid_status and phenotype set to `mixed (pooled sample)`, so donor identity needs demultiplexing. Patient and Donor numbers are separate namespaces - `Patient 29` and `Donor 29` are different subjects
residual_gaps: draw timing (day relative to admission or onset) is absent from the GEO record

verdict: CONFIRMED for grouping; suffix semantics CORRECTED
authoritative_patient_key: `patient` characteristic (P-M003); the title base S-M003 maps 1:1 onto it for all 284 samples
draw_meaning: progression / convalescence draws; 165 patients have 1 draw, 26 have 2, 5 have 3
anchor: symptom onset (per-sample day given in the record)
outcome_availability: `outcome` per sample (discharged 240, control 28, deceased 16) and it is unique within every one of the 196 patients
corrections: the numeric suffix is a sample index, not a draw index: 41 patient-days carry more than one library with identical sampling day, sample type, platform and batch (e.g. P-M003 has S-M003-2 and S-M003-3 both at day 25 from fresh sputum), while other suffixes do mark genuinely different draws (S-M003-1 at day 13). Group by patient + sampling day, not by suffix
residual_gaps: none material; sample types are heterogeneous (PBMC, sputum, sorted B cells) and should be filtered before cross-sample comparison

verdict: CONFIRMED for the repeat-draw pair; label mapping and one sample UNRESOLVED
authoritative_patient_key: `covid_5xx` token in the sample title (no patient field in the record)
draw_meaning: the paper's C1 was drawn at 9 days post symptom onset on supplemental oxygen and at 11 days following intubation - the only repeat draw in the study
outcome_availability: not in the GEO record; the paper's Fig. 1a clinical table is the source
corrections: GEO holds 7 COVID libraries (covid_555_1, covid_555_2, covid_556, covid_557, covid_558, covid_559, covid_561) plus 6 healthy controls (HIP*), i.e. 6 COVID patients - one short of the 8 samples from 7 patients the paper reports, with a gap in the numbering at covid_560
residual_gaps: the covid_5xx to C1-C7 mapping is not stated in the paper or the record, so per-patient clinical variables cannot be joined to the GSMs; the missing seventh patient's library is not in the deposit

verdict: SUPPORTED by metadata, not confirmable by label
authoritative_patient_key: no patient field exists; repeat draws are identifiable only as adjacent records with identical age and sex
draw_meaning: two draws at different times during hospitalization for three of the eight COVID-19 patients (paper: subjects C3, C6, C7)
outcome_availability: `subject status` per sample is a severity label scored on the day of sampling, not an outcome
corrections: exactly three adjacent duplicate age/sex pairs occur among the 11 nCoV samples - nCoV 3 & 4 (67 F), nCoV 7 & 8 (73 F), nCoV 9 & 10 (61 M) - matching the paper's three twice-sampled patients. The pair nCoV 9 / nCoV 10 carries different severity labels (severe, then mild) because severity was assessed on the day of each draw, so a label change within a patient is expected and is not evidence of mis-grouping
residual_gaps: the `nCoV n` to `Cn` mapping is not stated, so which pair is C3, C6 or C7 cannot be established; draw days are not reported per sample
